answer_1.quote: We collect annotations from both human annotators and two chat‑based VLMs... The final AbsVis dataset contains 10,125 human‑written concept‑explanation pairs across 675 images. In addition, we include 4,050 annotations generated by Qwen and Llava.
answer_1.outputs: concept–explanation pairs (abstract concept label and brief textual explanation)

answer_2.quote: We assess the semantic similarity of explanations of overlapping concepts using sentence transformers... we also compute pairwise cosine similarity between word2vec embeddings of concepts... explanation length (average number of words) and Spearman correlation between human and VLM preferences are reported.

answer_3.quote: We assess whether VLMs can be reliable evaluators for preferences, we compute the correlation between human and VLM preferences at both concept and explanation levels... Qwen shows slightly higher alignment with human preferences than Llava.
methods: correlation analysis between model and human preference scores

answer_4.quote: We recruited 220 participants via Prolific... For (a) concept preferences, participants assess which concept best and least represents the core idea of the image, and (b) for explanations, they assess which one best describes the image and which one provides the worst description... Best‑worst scaling (BWS) was used to collect comparative human judgments.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were shown an image with four candidate concepts (or concept‑explanation pairs) and asked to select the most and least representative/best and worst description.
